headline: The rotation became a liquidation: a Democratic midterm sweep repriced the AI buildout, SPX -4.4% and VIX +70% to 28 — and credit is the only thing still pretending.
summary: Yesterday the AI complex was the funding source for a rally. Today it is just the source. SPX -4.4% to 7353.7, NDX -6.4%, QQQ -6.5%, and QQQ/SPY -2.2% to z=-3.77 — the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. The epicenter is unchanged but the velocity is not: SMH -11.2% (-29.2% on the month, z=-3.35), MU -17.5%, AMD -17.3%, TSM -10.8%, AVGO -10.4% (0th percentile of its year), NVDA -9.3% and -24.1% on the month, ASML -9.3%, ORCL -6.9%. Asia paid the clearing price again — EWY -13.5%, EWT -11.5%, USDKRW +1.0% to 1357. The factor damage is cleaner than the index damage: high-beta/low-vol -7.0% today and -26.4% on the month at z=-4.05, growth/value -3.9% and -16.8% on the month at the 0th percentile, ARKK -9.0%, IPO -8.1%. Press coverage ties it to Democratic midterm gains and the implied regulatory and permitting risk around data centers; the power stack agrees — VST -6.2% (-29.7% on the month), GEV -7.5%, CEG -2.5%, GRID -6.3% and -17.5% on the month, NLR -4.0% at the 0th percentile.

The insurance gap I flagged yesterday closed in a single session, violently. VIX +69.7% to 28.18 (z=3.55, 84th percentile), VIX3M +35.9% to 25.55, and VIX/VIX3M at 1.1029 — the 100th percentile of the year, full backwardation. Note what did not move: SKEW actually fell 1.0% to 149.37. Tails were already paid for; this was the body of the distribution repricing. MOVE +4.3% to 97.9 and now 25% above its 200-day. The composites follow: credit & vol at -70 versus +12 yesterday, risk regime -20 versus -5.

And yet the median stock is fine. Equal-weight fell 2.9% against the cap-weighted 4.4%; RSP/SPY +1.6% to z=4.23 with acceleration 4.20, the most extreme breadth reading in the dataset. XLP -0.8%, XLU -0.7%, XLC -0.6%, KIE -0.6%, HD -1.5%, WMT -1.1% — and COST +1.8%, DHI +0.4%, GDX +1.4%, NEM +1.4%, KWEB +1.8%, FXI +1.0% closed green on a 4.4% down day. Credit barely flinched: HYG -0.3%, LQD +0.2%, BKLN -0.7% and still at the 88th percentile of its year. But the ratio is leading the price — HYG/IEF -0.6% to z=-2.15 and rolling over, -3.1% on the month. That is the single most important chart for the next two weeks: if HY starts discounting what equity vol already has, the breadth cushion goes.

The rates tape is the quiet warning. The front end did all the work — 2y -12bp to 4.46 (-33bp on the month), 5y -10bp to 4.59 (-44bp) — while the 30y gave back only 3bp to 5.25% and TLT managed +0.2%. Long duration did not hedge a 4.4% equity drawdown. 2s10s steepened 6bp to 0.38 with the 3m bill stuck at 4.17. That is a growth scare with sticky term premium, not a flight to quality. Commodities make it worse, not better: WTI +3.6% to 91.26 and Brent +5.0% to 99.32 (+63.2% YTD), gasoline +1.8%, even as copper -2.7%, copper/gold -3.3% and COPX -5.8% say the cycle is cooling. The cyclical industrials have already voted — CAT -35.7% on the month at z=-4.02, ETN -26.5%, PAVE -7.2%. Crypto confirmed the beta unwind: BTC -5.5% to 75,950, ETH -7.8%, SOL -6.6%, COIN -9.7% at the 0th percentile, MSTR -9.3%.

good.text: The front end is paying for the equity pain: 2y -12bp to 4.46 and -33bp on the month, 5y -44bp, 10y 4.84, 10y real yield down to 2.60 (-31bp on the month). Policy relief is being priced without a credit event.

Breadth is still absorbing the hit. Equal-weight -2.9% vs SPX -4.4%; RSP/SPY +1.6% to z=4.23 with acceleration 4.20, 94th percentile. Staples -0.8%, utilities -0.7%, communications -0.6% — the median stock is not in a bear market.
Credit refused to confirm: HYG -0.3%, LQD +0.2%, BKLN still at the 88th percentile of its 52-week range and flat on the month. As long as that holds, this is a dispersion event, not a solvency event.
The rate-sensitive consumer complex keeps leading: ITB +13.4% on the month and turning up, DHI +0.4% on the day, HD +22.1% on the month (z=3.07), XRT/SPY z=3.33, with the 30y mortgage -10bp to 7.18.

Gold miners are the only intact hedge: GDX +1.4% and NEM +1.4% against a -4.4% tape, gold +0.6% to 4098.9, GDX/gold +0.6% and turning up — with the metal still 9.1% below its 200-day, so the trade is not crowded.

Non-US ex-Asia is decoupling: DAX +4.7% on the month at the 97th percentile, India +7.0% (INDA rs +13.8% vs S&P), Mexico IPC +8.8% at the 95th percentile, EFA/SPY +4.7% on the month with acceleration 2.61.

bad.text: Volatility regime break: VIX +69.7% in one session to 28.18 (z=3.55), VIX3M +35.9% to 25.55, and VIX/VIX3M at 1.1029 — the 100th percentile of the year. Backwardation this deep forces systematic de-grossing regardless of fundamentals.

Semis are in free-fall and accelerating: SMH -11.2% (-29.2% on the month, acceleration z=-2.94), MU -17.5%, AMD -17.3%, TSM -10.8%, ASML -9.3%, with EWY -13.5% and EWT -11.5% and USDKRW +1.0% to 1357. SMH/SPY z=-3.99.

Oil is squeezing the wrong way: Brent +5.0% to 99.32 and WTI +3.6% to 91.26 (+58.9% YTD), gasoline +1.8%, on the same day the growth complex cracked. That is a margin and CPI problem, not a reflation signal — CPI index is +106bp YTD.

Long duration failed as a hedge. The 30y fell only 3bp to 5.25% and TLT managed +0.2% against a 4.4% equity drawdown; 2s10s steepened 6bp; MOVE +4.3% to 97.9, 25% above its 200-day. Term premium is not cooperating with the Fed-cut trade.

The cycle proxies are already in a recession tape: copper -2.7% and copper/gold -3.3%, COPX -5.8%, FCX -7.5%, XME -16.5% on the month, CAT -35.7% on the month at z=-4.02, ETN -26.5%, PAVE -7.2%, industrials/utilities z=-2.28.

Credit's leading ratio is already rolling: HYG/IEF -0.6% to z=-2.15, -3.1% on the month. Add crypto as the canary — BTC -5.5% to 75,950, ETH -7.8%, COIN -9.7% at the 0th percentile, MSTR -9.3% — and the risk appetite bid is gone.

trades.name: High yield is the last domino
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF; or buy Dec HYG put spreads
trades.expr: Short HYG against a dollar-neutral long in IEF, or buy HYG Dec 76/72 put spreads for ~1.2% of notional. Size the options version if you want convexity rather than carry drag.
trades.thesis: Equity vol has fully repriced (VIX 28.18, z=3.55) while HY is flat on the month and only 1.2% below its 200-day. The ratio is leading the price: HYG/IEF is already z=-2.15 and rolling over, -3.1% on the month. In every prior AI-capex scare, credit lagged by one to two weeks and then caught down in a single gap. Index-level dispersion this extreme (high-beta/low-vol -26.4% on the month) does not stay quarantined in equity.
trades.trigger: Credit & vol composite collapsed to -70 from +12 yesterday; HYG -0.3% and BKLN -0.7% on a day SPX fell 4.4%, with HYG/IEF -0.6%.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF reclaims 0.855 and VIX closes below 20 with the term structure back under 1.00 — that means the equity event stayed an equity event.
trades.target: HYG 74 (-4%), HYG/IEF toward 0.80; options version targets a 3x on the spread.

trades.name: 2s30s bull steepener
trades.line: Long 2y futures vs short 30y — the front end does the work
trades.expr: Long TU (2y note futures) vs short WN/UB, duration-weighted roughly 5:1; swap equivalent is receive 2y vs pay 30y.
trades.thesis: The market is pricing cuts, not safety. The 2y has fallen 33bp on the month to 4.46 and 12bp today, while the 30y gave back 3bp and sits at 5.25% with TLT up only 0.2% on a 4.4% equity decline. Term premium is sticky — MOVE +4.3% to 97.9, breakevens only 2.24, the 30y mortgage still 7.18, and the CPI index +106bp YTD. A growth scare plus an unchanged fiscal picture steepens; it does not bull-flatten.
trades.trigger: 2s10s +6bp to 0.38 on the single worst equity day of the year, with the 3m bill anchored at 4.17 (-4bp on the month) and 3m10y down 39bp on the month.
trades.stop: 2s10s back below 25bp, or a long-end rally that drags the 30y under 5.00% while the 2y stalls.

trades.name: Energy equity catches up to $99 Brent
trades.line: Long XOP — crude +5% while E&Ps sold off 2.9%
trades.expr: Long XOP 60% / XLE 40%, hedged with a half-weight SPY short to strip index beta out of a high-vol tape.
trades.thesis: Yesterday energy equity capitulated to crude on an up day for oil; today crude ripped again and the equity still fell. Brent is 99.32 (+63.2% YTD, 6.9% above its 200-day) and WTI 91.26, yet XOP is only 2.3% above its 200-day and XOM/CVX are up just 0.5% and 2.6% on the month. Energy is one of three sectors with positive 3-month relative strength (XLE rs +11.5%) and it is the natural beneficiary if the new Washington balance slows permitting for everything except what is already producing.
trades.trigger: Brent +5.0% and WTI +3.6% today against XLE -3.0%, XOP -2.9%, OIH -5.0%; oil/gold +2.9% and +23.9% over three months.
trades.stop: Brent closes below 90 (gives back the whole squeeze) or XOP breaks 160.
trades.target: XOP 195 (+12%); XLE back to the 0.70 relative-strength highs.

trades.name: Gold miners, the only working hedge
trades.line: Long GDX / Jan calls — green on a -4.4% S&P day
trades.expr: Long GDX outright, or GDX January 90 calls; optional overlay short GLD at 50% notional to isolate the operating-leverage repricing.
trades.thesis: Miners outperformed the metal two sessions running and the metal itself is not crowded — gold 4098.9 sits at the 14th percentile of its 52-week range and 9.1% below its 200-day after a -5.6% YTD. GDX/gold is turning up (+6.0% over three months), which historically precedes a multi-month leg. With the 10y real yield down 31bp on the month to 2.60 and the front end pricing cuts, the discount-rate headwind is gone while the equity hedge value is proven.
trades.trigger: GDX +1.4% and NEM +1.4% with gold +0.6% on a session where SPX fell 4.4% and every other cyclical hedge failed.
trades.stop: Gold below 3950 or GDX below 80 — that would mean miners are just high-beta equity after all.

trades.name: Short the crypto-equity premium
trades.line: Short MSTR vs long IBIT — stop paying for the wrapper
trades.expr: Short MSTR $1.00 against long IBIT ~$0.55 notional to beta-match; roll monthly.
trades.thesis: The levered crypto proxies are de-rating faster than the asset they hold. MSTR is -21.4% on the month against BTC -8.8%; COIN is -26.3% on the month and sits at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. In a de-grossing regime, the premium on balance-sheet leverage compresses first and does not recover until spot makes a new high. IBIT gives you the spot exposure with none of the financing risk.
trades.trigger: MSTR -9.3% and COIN -9.7% today versus BTC -5.5% and IBIT -5.1%; ETH -7.8% and ETH/BTC -2.3% confirm the beta unwind rather than a dollar move (DXY +0.1%).
trades.stop: MSTR outperforms BTC by 10% over any two-week window, or BTC reclaims 85,000 with the premium expanding.

trades.name: Fade the VIX term-structure panic
trades.line: Short Dec VIX vs long Mar; or sell 1m SPX put spreads
trades.expr: Short December VIX futures against long March VIX futures (calendar), or sell SPX 1-month 8-12% OTM put spreads. Small size — this is the one trade in the book that is short the tape.
trades.thesis: VIX/VIX3M at 1.1029 is the 100th percentile of the year and a 24.8% one-day jump. Backwardation that deep without a credit event has historically been a two-to-four week mean-reverter, and the hedges are already bought: SKEW fell 1.0% to 149.37 today, so tail demand did not expand — only spot vol did. Pair this with the HYG short above and you are long the real risk and short the panic premium.
trades.trigger: VIX +69.7% in one session to 28.18 (z=3.55) while HYG fell only 0.3% and LQD rose 0.2%.
trades.stop: VIX3M above 32, or HYG/IEF below 0.82 — credit confirming means the curve stays inverted and you are wrong.

trades.name: Housing gets the cuts before chips do
trades.line: Long ITB — rate relief lands on homebuilders first
trades.expr: Long ITB, or DHI outright; finance it by shorting XLI, which is -11.8% over three months with relative strength down.
trades.thesis: The only cyclical group with improving absolute and relative trend is housing. ITB is +13.4% on the month and turning up, XHB/SPY is z=2.47, DHI closed green today and is +15.3% on the month, and HD is +22.1% on the month at z=3.07. The 5y yield is -44bp on the month and the 30y mortgage has finally started to follow, -10bp to 7.18. If the front end is right about cuts, this is where the earnings revisions happen, and it has zero AI-capex exposure.
trades.trigger: DHI +0.4% and the ITB complex outperformed by more than 270bp on a -4.4% index day; XHB/SPY +1.0% today with acceleration z=2.37.
trades.stop: 30y mortgage back above 7.40% or ITB below 92.
